items.meaning: Someone or something that is extremely valuable and beneficial to a team or organization.
items.example: Your ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously makes you a real asset to the team.
items.plain: Your ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously makes you very valuable to the team.
items.note: Strong praise, often used in professional contexts to highlight someone's significant contribution.

items.meaning: Performed better than what was anticipated or hoped for.
items.example: The presentation you gave yesterday truly exceeded expectations; everyone was very impressed.
items.plain: The presentation you gave yesterday was much better than we expected; everyone was very impressed.
items.note: Common in performance reviews or when acknowledging outstanding work.

items.meaning: Deserving of strong praise and approval.
items.example: Your initiative in taking on that extra responsibility was highly commendable.
items.plain: Your initiative in taking on that extra responsibility was very praiseworthy.
items.note: Formal and appreciative, often used for actions showing good judgment or effort.

items.meaning: An expression of praise for completing a task successfully and to a good standard.
items.example: I just wanted to say, a job well done on the quarterly report; it was very thorough.
items.plain: I just wanted to say, you did a good job on the quarterly report; it was very thorough.
items.note: Simple, direct praise, suitable for various professional and informal settings.

items.meaning: Especially successful in producing a desired or intended result.
items.example: Your strategy for engaging the new clients was particularly effective.
items.plain: Your strategy for engaging the new clients was very successful.
items.note: Specific praise, highlighting a successful method or approach.

items.meaning: To express formal praise or approval for someone's actions or achievements.
items.example: I wanted to commend you on how you handled that difficult client meeting.
items.plain: I wanted to praise you for how you handled that difficult client meeting.
items.note: A polite and slightly formal way to give specific praise.

items.meaning: To feel grateful or thankful for something.
items.example: I really appreciate you staying late to help finish the proposal.
items.plain: I am very grateful that you stayed late to help finish the proposal.
items.note: Sincere and common way to express gratitude for effort or help.

items.meaning: To evoke a strong emotional response or resonate with someone's feelings or beliefs.
items.example: Your opening remarks in the presentation really struck a chord with the audience.
items.plain: Your opening remarks in the presentation really resonated with the audience.
items.note: Implies a deep connection or understanding, often used for impactful communication.

items.meaning: Acknowledging someone's contribution or success, even if it's unexpected or from a rival.
items.example: Credit where credit's due, Sarah's innovative idea significantly improved our workflow.
items.plain: Sarah's innovative idea significantly improved our workflow, and she deserves recognition for it.
items.note: Used to ensure proper recognition, often when the person might otherwise be overlooked.

items.meaning: To establish a very high standard of quality or achievement.
items.example: Your meticulous attention to detail on this project has really set a high bar for future work.
items.plain: Your meticulous attention to detail on this project has established a very high standard for future work.
items.note: Praises excellence and implies it serves as a benchmark for others.

items.meaning: A minor worry or apprehension about something.
items.example: I have a slight concern about the timeline for the next phase of the project.
items.plain: I have a minor worry about the timeline for the next phase of the project.
items.note: A soft, diplomatic way to introduce a potential problem or issue.

items.meaning: A gentle way to suggest an alternative approach or idea.
items.example: Perhaps we could consider integrating a different software solution for better efficiency.
items.plain: Maybe we should integrate a different software solution for better efficiency.
items.note: Polite and collaborative, inviting discussion rather than dictating.

items.meaning: Suggesting that an idea or option should be investigated further.
items.example: It might be worth exploring alternative marketing channels for this product.
items.plain: We should probably investigate alternative marketing channels for this product.
items.note: Tentative and open-ended, encouraging further thought and research.

items.meaning: A specific aspect or skill that could be improved or enhanced.
items.example: I think one area for development could be your public speaking skills.
items.plain: I think your public speaking skills could be improved.
items.note: A common, polite, and professional euphemism for a weakness or flaw.

items.meaning: To speak honestly and directly, sometimes implying a difficult truth.
items.example: To be perfectly frank, the initial proposal lacked a clear strategic direction.
items.plain: Honestly, the initial proposal lacked a clear strategic direction.
items.note: Signals directness; can sound a little blunt if not softened by tone.

items.meaning: A polite but firm way to express disagreement, often before stating a contrasting opinion.
items.example: With all due respect, I don't think that approach will yield the desired results.
items.plain: I respectfully disagree; I don't think that approach will yield the desired results.
items.note: Used to challenge an idea or person politely, but clearly. Can be slightly confrontational.

items.meaning: To have some doubts or reservations about something, not fully believing it.
items.example: I'm not entirely convinced that the new policy will be effective in practice.
items.plain: I have some doubts that the new policy will be effective in practice.
items.note: A polite and understated way to express disagreement or skepticism.

items.meaning: To state the single main doubt or concern one has about something.
items.example: My only reservation is the tight deadline for implementing these changes.
items.plain: My main concern is the tight deadline for implementing these changes.
items.note: Clearly identifies the primary sticking point without dismissing the whole idea.

items.meaning: Something important to remember or consider.
items.example: It's worth bearing in mind that our budget for this quarter is quite limited.
items.plain: Remember that our budget for this quarter is quite limited.
items.note: A gentle reminder or a subtle warning about a factor to consider.

items.meaning: To propose an idea or course of action in a soft, non-forceful manner.
items.example: I'd like to gently suggest a different approach to managing client expectations.
items.plain: I'd like to politely propose a different approach to managing client expectations.
items.note: Emphasizes a soft, non-confrontational delivery of advice or criticism.

items.meaning: A specific issue or topic that causes disagreement or argument.
items.example: The allocation of resources became a point of contention during the team meeting.
items.plain: The allocation of resources caused disagreement during the team meeting.
items.note: Describes a specific area of dispute, often used in formal discussions.

items.meaning: Has the potential to be improved or made more precise and elegant.
items.example: The initial draft of the proposal could be refined to present a stronger argument.
items.plain: The initial draft of the proposal could be improved to present a stronger argument.
items.note: A polite and constructive way to suggest improvements without being overly critical.

items.meaning: Requires some small adjustments or fine-tuning to improve it.
items.example: The presentation is good, but it needs a bit of tweaking to fit the new branding guidelines.
items.plain: The presentation is good, but it needs some small adjustments to fit the new branding guidelines.
items.note: Informal and gentle way to suggest minor improvements.

items.text: something to keep an eye on
items.form: something to keep an eye on
items.meaning: An issue or situation that requires continuous monitoring or attention.
items.example: The fluctuating market trends are something to keep an eye on for our next investment.
items.plain: We should continuously monitor the fluctuating market trends for our next investment.
items.note: A subtle warning or reminder to remain vigilant about a particular matter.

items.meaning: To feel slightly unwilling or reluctant to do or agree with something.
items.example: I'm a little hesitant about committing to such a tight deadline without more resources.
items.plain: I'm slightly unwilling to commit to such a tight deadline without more resources.
items.note: Expresses mild reluctance or caution, often used to voice a concern politely.

items.meaning: To express an idea or realization that has just occurred to you.
items.example: It strikes me that we haven't fully considered the long-term implications of this decision.
items.plain: I just realized that we haven't fully considered the long-term implications of this decision.
items.note: Introduces a personal observation or insight, often used to offer a new perspective.

items.meaning: To introduce one's personal opinion or perspective on a matter.
items.example: The way I see it, we need to prioritize customer satisfaction above all else.
items.plain: In my opinion, we need to prioritize customer satisfaction above all else.
items.note: Common and direct way to state one's viewpoint, inviting discussion.

items.meaning: To clarify the main point or intention behind what one is saying.
items.example: What I'm getting at is that we need a more cohesive strategy across departments.
items.plain: My main point is that we need a more cohesive strategy across departments.
items.note: Used to summarize or make explicit the underlying message, especially after a lengthy explanation.

items.meaning: To clarify a misunderstanding by stating what is not the case before explaining what is.
items.example: It's not so much that I disagree with the goal, but rather the proposed method.
items.plain: I don't disagree with the goal; instead, I disagree with the proposed method.
items.note: Useful for nuanced feedback, distinguishing between different aspects of an issue.

items.meaning: To indicate that what you are saying is an understatement, and the reality is more extreme.
items.example: To put it mildly, the project encountered some significant challenges.
items.plain: The project encountered many significant challenges, and that's an understatement.
items.note: Often used with a touch of irony or dry humor to describe a difficult situation.

items.meaning: A polite and indirect way to express disagreement.
items.example: I'm afraid I don't quite agree with your assessment of the market trends.
items.plain: I politely disagree with your assessment of the market trends.
items.note: Softens direct disagreement, making it less confrontational.

items.meaning: To present an alternative viewpoint or way of looking at a situation.
items.example: I'd like to offer a different perspective on how we might approach this problem.
items.plain: I'd like to present an alternative viewpoint on how we might approach this problem.
items.note: Collaborative and non-confrontational, inviting consideration of other ideas.

items.meaning: To suggest going back to reconsider or discuss something again.
items.example: We might want to revisit the budget allocations before finalizing the plan.
items.plain: We should reconsider the budget allocations before finalizing the plan.
items.note: A gentle suggestion to re-evaluate a decision or topic.

items.meaning: To introduce a point that is open to debate or discussion, often a critical one.
items.example: It could be argued that the current strategy isn't sustainable in the long term.
items.plain: Someone might say that the current strategy isn't sustainable in the long term.
items.note: Impersonal and academic, used to present a critical point without owning it directly.

items.meaning: A sensitive issue that requires careful handling and tact.
items.example: Discussing salary adjustments is always a delicate matter.
items.plain: Discussing salary adjustments is always a sensitive issue.
items.note: Emphasizes the need for careful communication due to sensitivity.

items.meaning: To proceed with caution and sensitivity, especially in a difficult situation.
items.example: We need to tread carefully when giving feedback to new team members.
items.plain: We need to be very careful when giving feedback to new team members.
items.note: Advises prudence and circumspection in actions or words.

items.meaning: A detailed analysis and assessment of something, intended to be helpful and improve it.
items.example: I'd like to offer a constructive critique of your project proposal.
items.plain: I'd like to offer helpful feedback on your project proposal.
items.note: Emphasizes that the criticism is intended to build up, not tear down.

items.meaning: Something that provides material for careful consideration or reflection.
items.example: Your presentation gave us a lot of food for thought regarding our future strategy.
items.plain: Your presentation gave us a lot to think about regarding our future strategy.
items.note: Suggests that an idea or information is valuable for contemplation.

items.meaning: After careful thought or consideration.
items.example: On reflection, I think we should have allocated more time for the testing phase.
items.plain: After careful thought, I think we should have allocated more time for the testing phase.
items.note: Introduces a revised opinion or realization after further consideration.

items.meaning: With the advantage of knowing how an event turned out.
items.example: In hindsight, launching the product during the holiday season was not the best decision.
items.plain: Knowing what we know now, launching the product during the holiday season was not the best decision.
items.note: Used to comment on past events with the benefit of present knowledge.

items.meaning: A situation or experience from which one can gain knowledge or skills.
items.example: While the project didn't go as planned, it was certainly a learning opportunity.
items.plain: While the project didn't go as planned, we certainly learned a lot from it.
items.note: A positive reframing of a mistake or failure, emphasizing growth.

items.meaning: Aspects of something that can be made better.
items.example: There's always room for improvement, even in a successful project.
items.plain: Even in a successful project, there are always things that can be made better.
items.note: A polite and common way to suggest that something is not perfect.

items.meaning: A small or less important detail or issue.
items.example: That's a minor point, but it's worth clarifying before we proceed.
items.plain: That's a small detail, but it's worth clarifying before we proceed.
items.note: Used to downplay the significance of a criticism, making it easier to accept.

items.meaning: A reasonable and well-founded argument or observation.
items.example: You've raised a valid point about the potential impact on our budget.
items.plain: You've raised a reasonable argument about the potential impact on our budget.
items.note: Acknowledges the merit of someone else's argument, even if you don't fully agree.

items.meaning: Used to introduce a mitigating factor or a balanced perspective, often after criticism.
items.example: To be fair, the team was working under immense pressure and a tight deadline.
items.plain: It's important to consider that the team was working under immense pressure and a tight deadline.
items.note: Often used to defend someone or provide context for a situation.

items.meaning: Used to introduce a piece of advice or opinion that may or may not be helpful.
items.example: For what it's worth, I think a direct approach might be more effective here.
items.plain: I think a direct approach might be more effective here, though you may not agree.
items.note: Hedges an opinion, making it less forceful and easier to accept or reject.

items.meaning: To state that one will be concise and not speak for long.
items.example: I'll keep it brief, but I wanted to highlight a few key takeaways from the meeting.
items.plain: I will speak briefly, but I wanted to highlight a few key takeaways from the meeting.
items.note: A common opening to signal conciseness, often used when giving feedback.

items.meaning: To bring up an issue or worry for discussion.
items.example: I wanted to raise a concern about the security protocols for the new system.
items.plain: I wanted to mention a worry about the security protocols for the new system.
items.note: A polite and professional way to introduce a problem or worry.

items.meaning: To acknowledge and understand someone's point of view, even if you don't fully agree.
items.example: I hear what you're saying about the workload, and I'll see what adjustments we can make.
items.plain: I understand your point about the workload, and I'll see what adjustments we can make.
items.note: Shows active listening and empathy, often used before offering a solution or counterpoint.

items.meaning: To acknowledge and accept the validity of someone's argument or statement.
items.example: I take your point about the need for more data before making a final decision.
items.plain: I accept your argument about the need for more data before making a final decision.
items.note: Indicates understanding and acceptance of a specific argument.

items.meaning: To be grateful for someone's honesty and directness, especially when it's difficult.
items.example: I appreciate your candor in pointing out the flaws in my presentation.
items.plain: I am grateful for your honesty in pointing out the flaws in my presentation.
items.note: Acknowledges and values direct, honest feedback, even if it's critical.

items.meaning: To accept and consider a suggestion or criticism seriously.
items.example: That's a very helpful suggestion; I'll take that on board for future projects.
items.plain: That's a very helpful suggestion; I'll consider it seriously for future projects.
items.note: Common in British English; means to absorb and act upon advice.

items.meaning: An evaluation or judgment that is reasonable and unbiased.
items.example: I think that's a fair assessment of the project's challenges and successes.
items.plain: I think that's a reasonable judgment of the project's challenges and successes.
items.note: Indicates agreement with the accuracy and impartiality of the feedback.

items.meaning: To acknowledge that someone has brought up a reasonable and important issue.
items.example: You've raised a valid point about the potential impact on our budget.
items.plain: You've brought up a reasonable and important issue about the potential impact on our budget.
items.note: Acknowledges the merit of someone else's argument, even if you don't fully agree.

items.text: I see where you're coming from
items.form: I see where you're coming from
items.meaning: To understand the reasons or motivations behind someone's opinion or actions.
items.example: I see where you're coming from regarding the need for more resources.
items.plain: I understand your reasons for needing more resources.
items.note: Shows empathy and understanding of another's perspective.

items.meaning: To be willing to consider new ideas or advice from others.
items.example: I'm open to suggestions on how we can improve our team's communication.
items.plain: I am willing to consider new ideas on how we can improve our team's communication.
items.note: Signals receptiveness to feedback and a collaborative attitude.

items.meaning: To remember something important and consider it in the future.
items.example: Thank you for the advice; I'll bear that in mind when planning the next phase.
items.plain: Thank you for the advice; I'll remember it when planning the next phase.
items.note: A polite way to acknowledge advice and promise to consider it.

items.meaning: A standard and polite way to express gratitude for receiving comments or criticism.
items.example: Thank you for the feedback on my performance review; I found it very helpful.
items.plain: I appreciate the comments on my performance review; I found them very helpful.
items.note: Essential for showing professionalism and receptiveness to input.

items.meaning: To investigate or examine a matter further.
items.example: You've mentioned a discrepancy in the data; I'll look into that right away.
items.plain: You've mentioned a discrepancy in the data; I'll investigate it right away.
items.note: A common promise to take action and investigate an issue.

items.text: I'll make a note of that
items.form: I'll make a note of that
items.meaning: To write down or mentally register a piece of information for future reference.
items.example: That's an important detail; I'll make a note of that for the project plan.
items.plain: That's an important detail; I'll write it down for the project plan.
items.note: Indicates that the information is considered important and will be remembered.

items.meaning: To think carefully about a suggestion or idea before making a decision.
items.example: Your proposal for the new marketing campaign is interesting; I'll consider that.
items.plain: Your proposal for the new marketing campaign is interesting; I'll think about it carefully.
items.note: A polite way to acknowledge a suggestion without immediately committing to it.

items.meaning: To think deeply and carefully about something.
items.example: I need some time to process your comments; I'll reflect on that over the weekend.
items.plain: I need some time to process your comments; I'll think deeply about them over the weekend.
items.note: Suggests a more profound and thoughtful consideration than simply "thinking about it."

items.meaning: To promise to consider an idea or suggestion carefully.
items.example: That's an interesting perspective; I'll give that some thought.
items.plain: That's an interesting perspective; I'll think about it carefully.
items.note: Similar to "I'll consider that," but perhaps implies a slightly longer period of consideration.

items.meaning: To accept blame or accountability for a mistake or negative outcome.
items.example: The error in the report was mine; I'll take responsibility for that.
items.plain: The error in the report was mine; I'll accept the blame for it.
items.note: Crucial for demonstrating accountability and professionalism.

items.meaning: To deal with a problem or issue directly and promptly.
items.example: You've pointed out a flaw in the process; I'll address that with the team.
items.plain: You've pointed out a flaw in the process; I'll deal with it with the team.
items.note: A commitment to take action to resolve a specific issue.

items.meaning: To continue to monitor or take further action regarding a matter.
items.example: I'll follow up on that client inquiry first thing tomorrow morning.
items.plain: I'll continue to monitor that client inquiry first thing tomorrow morning.
items.note: Promises further action or communication regarding an ongoing issue.

items.meaning: To return to a topic or issue later, often after gathering more information or taking action.
items.example: I need to check with legal first, but I'll circle back on that question by end of day.
items.plain: I need to check with legal first, but I'll get back to you on that question by end of day.
items.note: Common in corporate settings, implies a return to a discussion after an interim step.

items.meaning: To start working on something immediately.
items.example: Thanks for flagging the urgent issue; I'll get right on that.
items.plain: Thanks for flagging the urgent issue; I'll start working on it immediately.
items.note: Conveys urgency and a commitment to immediate action.

items.text: I'll get to the bottom of that
items.form: I'll get to the bottom of that
items.meaning: To discover the true reason or cause of something, especially a problem.
items.example: There seems to be a misunderstanding; I'll get to the bottom of that.
items.plain: There seems to be a misunderstanding; I'll find out the true reason for it.
items.note: Implies a commitment to thorough investigation to resolve an issue.

items.meaning: To arrange or resolve a problem or situation.
items.example: Don't worry about the scheduling conflict; I'll get it sorted.
items.plain: Don't worry about the scheduling conflict; I'll resolve it.
items.note: Common in British English, means to fix or organize something.

items.meaning: To complete a task or project.
items.example: Leave it with me; I'll get it done by the deadline.
items.plain: Leave it with me; I'll complete it by the deadline.
items.note: A direct and confident promise to complete a task.

items.meaning: To repair something that is broken or incorrect.
items.example: The bug in the software is annoying, but I'll get it fixed.
items.plain: The bug in the software is annoying, but I'll repair it.
items.note: A direct promise to correct a problem.

items.meaning: To ensure that something is correct or done properly.
items.example: I made a mistake on the last report, but I promise I'll get it right this time.
items.plain: I made a mistake on the last report, but I promise I'll do it correctly this time.
items.note: Expresses a commitment to accuracy and improvement.

items.meaning: To promise to take specific action to ensure something happens.
items.example: I'll make sure to include your feedback in the next revision of the document.
items.plain: I promise to include your feedback in the next revision of the document.
items.note: A strong commitment to ensure a particular action is taken.

items.meaning: To regularly inform someone about developments or progress.
items.example: I'll look into that issue and I'll keep you posted on my findings.
items.plain: I'll look into that issue and I'll regularly inform you about my findings.
items.note: Common and informal way to promise updates.

items.meaning: To promise to definitely do something.
items.example: I'll be sure to consider your suggestions for the new project.
items.plain: I promise I will definitely consider your suggestions for the new project.
items.note: A strong assurance that an action will be taken.

items.meaning: To promise to make the greatest possible effort to achieve something.
items.example: I'll do my best to incorporate all the feedback into the final design.
items.plain: I'll make the greatest possible effort to incorporate all the feedback into the final design.
items.note: Expresses commitment and effort, acknowledging potential difficulty.

items.meaning: To reply or respond to someone at a later time.
items.example: I need to check my calendar, but I'll get back to you with a suitable time.
items.plain: I need to check my calendar, but I'll reply to you with a suitable time.
items.note: A standard way to promise a future response or update.

items.meaning: To introduce good news or a positive observation.
items.example: I'm pleased to say your recent performance has been outstanding.
items.plain: I'm happy to tell you your recent performance has been outstanding.
items.note: A polite and positive opening, often used when giving praise.

items.meaning: To introduce positive information or an encouraging update.
items.example: I'm happy to report that the client was very satisfied with your work.
items.plain: I'm glad to tell you that the client was very satisfied with your work.
items.note: Formal and positive, used to deliver good news or positive feedback.

items.meaning: To express strong belief in a positive outcome or ability.
items.example: I'm confident that you'll excel in this new role.
items.plain: I strongly believe that you'll excel in this new role.
items.note: Expresses trust and belief in someone's capabilities, often used in praise.

items.meaning: To express admiration for someone's qualities or achievements.
items.example: I'm impressed by your dedication to improving the project's efficiency.
items.plain: I admire your dedication to improving the project's efficiency.
items.note: Direct and sincere praise, highlighting a specific positive trait or action.

items.meaning: To express strong admiration for a specific aspect of someone's work or character.
items.example: I'm particularly impressed with how you managed to resolve that complex issue.
items.plain: I'm very impressed with how you managed to resolve that complex issue.
items.note: Emphasizes specific, high-level praise for a notable achievement.

items.meaning: To express great pleasure or satisfaction about something observed.
items.example: I'm delighted to see the progress you've made on your professional development goals.
items.plain: I'm very pleased to see the progress you've made on your professional development goals.
items.note: Conveys strong positive emotion, often for visible improvements or achievements.

items.meaning: To express strong satisfaction with something.
items.example: I'm very pleased with the outcome of the negotiation; well done.
items.plain: I'm very satisfied with the outcome of the negotiation; well done.
items.note: Direct and clear expression of satisfaction, often for results.

items.meaning: To express a good level of satisfaction, often with a hint of understatement.
items.example: I'm quite happy with the initial results, though there's always room for refinement.
items.plain: I'm fairly satisfied with the initial results, though there's always room for refinement.
items.note: Polite and slightly understated, suggesting satisfaction without being overly effusive.

items.meaning: To express mild dissatisfaction or reservation about something.
items.example: I'm not entirely happy with the current timeline for project completion.
items.plain: I'm slightly dissatisfied with the current timeline for project completion.
items.note: A polite and indirect way to express dissatisfaction, softening the criticism.

items.meaning: To express a minor worry or apprehension.
items.example: I'm a bit concerned about the lack of communication between the two teams.
items.plain: I'm slightly worried about the lack of communication between the two teams.
items.note: A gentle way to introduce a concern, making it less confrontational.

items.meaning: To politely introduce bad news or a negative observation.
items.example: I'm afraid that the proposed solution might not be feasible within our budget.
items.plain: Unfortunately, the proposed solution might not be feasible within our budget.
items.note: Softens negative feedback or news, making it sound more empathetic.

items.meaning: To express regret before delivering unwelcome news or criticism.
items.example: I'm sorry to say that the report contains several factual errors.
items.plain: Unfortunately, the report contains several factual errors.
items.note: A polite and empathetic way to deliver negative feedback or news.

items.meaning: To express uncertainty or doubt, often as a gentle way to question an idea.
items.example: I'm not sure if this approach aligns with our long-term strategic goals.
items.plain: I doubt if this approach aligns with our long-term strategic goals.
items.note: Hedges a critical point, making it less direct and more open to discussion.

items.meaning: To politely introduce a question or a suggestion, often implying a concern.
items.example: I'm wondering if we've fully considered all the risks involved in this venture.
items.plain: I'm asking if we've fully considered all the risks involved in this venture.
items.note: A soft and indirect way to raise a point or express a doubt.

items.meaning: To express a tentative opinion or belief.
items.example: I'm inclined to think that a different strategy would yield better results.
items.plain: I tend to believe that a different strategy would yield better results.
items.note: A polite and slightly formal way to offer an opinion without being assertive.

items.meaning: To state one's belief or judgment, often in a formal context.
items.example: I'm of the opinion that we should prioritize quality over speed for this project.
items.plain: I believe that we should prioritize quality over speed for this project.
items.note: A formal way to express a strong opinion, often in a professional discussion.

items.meaning: To express a strong dedication to a course of action or goal.
items.example: I'm committed to improving my time management skills based on your advice.
items.plain: I'm dedicated to improving my time management skills based on your advice.
items.note: Shows strong resolve and dedication, often in response to constructive criticism.

items.meaning: To express a strong intention to achieve something despite difficulties.
items.example: I'm determined to address these issues and ensure they don't recur.
items.plain: I strongly intend to address these issues and ensure they don't recur.
items.note: Conveys strong willpower and resolve to overcome challenges.

items.meaning: To express sincere thanks for something.
items.example: I'm grateful for your honest assessment of my performance.
items.plain: I'm thankful for your honest assessment of my performance.
items.note: A sincere way to express appreciation for feedback, especially critical.

items.meaning: To express appreciation for something received or experienced.
items.example: I'm thankful for the opportunity to discuss these points with you.
items.plain: I appreciate the opportunity to discuss these points with you.
items.note: A common and polite way to express gratitude.

items.meaning: To express willingness to explain something further.
items.example: I'm happy to clarify any points in the report that were unclear.
items.plain: I'm willing to explain any points in the report that were unclear.
items.note: A polite offer to provide more detail or explanation.

items.meaning: To express preparedness to take action.
items.example: I'm ready to implement the changes you suggested immediately.
items.plain: I'm prepared to implement the changes you suggested immediately.
items.note: Conveys readiness and willingness to act on feedback.

items.meaning: To express strong eagerness or enthusiasm to do something.
items.example: I'm keen to learn more about how I can improve in this area.
items.plain: I'm eager to learn more about how I can improve in this area.
items.note: Common in British English, shows enthusiasm and a proactive attitude.

items.meaning: To express anticipation and excitement for a future event or action.
items.example: I'm looking forward to putting your advice into practice.
items.plain: I'm excited about putting your advice into practice.
items.note: Conveys a positive and proactive attitude towards future actions.

items.meaning: To express strong belief in the collective ability to achieve something.
items.example: I'm confident we can overcome these challenges with a revised strategy.
items.plain: I strongly believe we can overcome these challenges with a revised strategy.
items.note: Builds team morale and expresses optimism in collective problem-solving.

items.meaning: To express certainty about a fact or outcome.
items.example: I'm sure that with a bit more effort, we'll achieve our targets.
items.plain: I'm certain that with a bit more effort, we'll achieve our targets.
items.note: Conveys conviction and reassurance, often used to motivate.

items.meaning: To express satisfaction upon receiving positive information.
items.example: I'm pleased to hear that the new process is already showing positive results.
items.plain: I'm happy to hear that the new process is already showing positive results.
items.note: A polite way to acknowledge and appreciate good news or positive feedback.

items.meaning: To express satisfaction or relief at learning something.
items.example: I'm glad to know that my efforts are making a positive impact.
items.plain: I'm happy to learn that my efforts are making a positive impact.
items.note: Conveys appreciation for being informed, often about positive outcomes.

items.meaning: To express willingness to assist or provide support.
items.example: If you need any assistance with implementing these changes, I'm happy to help.
items.plain: If you need any assistance with implementing these changes, I'm willing to help.
items.note: A common and polite offer of assistance, fostering collaboration.

items.meaning: To express one's availability and intention to provide assistance.
items.example: Remember, I'm here to support you through any challenges you face.
items.plain: Remember, I'm available to assist you through any challenges you face.
items.note: Offers reassurance and practical help, building trust.

items.meaning: To express continuous receptiveness to new ideas, feedback, or learning.
items.example: I'm always open to constructive criticism that helps me grow.
items.plain: I'm always receptive to constructive criticism that helps me grow.
items.note: Signals a growth mindset and willingness to learn from others.

items.meaning: To express strong interest in listening to someone's thoughts or opinions.
items.example: I'm keen to hear your thoughts on how we can improve this process.
items.plain: I'm eager to hear your thoughts on how we can improve this process.
items.note: Shows active engagement and values others' input.

items.meaning: To express a proactive search for methods to achieve improvement.
items.example: I'm looking for ways to enhance our team's productivity and collaboration.
items.plain: I'm searching for methods to enhance our team's productivity and collaboration.
items.note: Indicates a proactive and improvement-oriented mindset.

items.meaning: To state one's objective or goal.
items.example: I'm aiming to complete the revised proposal by the end of the week.
items.plain: My goal is to complete the revised proposal by the end of the week.
items.note: Clearly states an intention or target, often in response to feedback.

items.meaning: To indicate that one is currently engaged in improving or developing something.
items.example: I'm working on improving my presentation skills, as you suggested.
items.plain: I'm currently developing my presentation skills, as you suggested.
items.note: Shows that feedback has been acted upon and progress is underway.

items.meaning: To report that one is advancing in a task or area of development.
items.example: I'm making progress on the new client report, and it's nearly complete.
items.plain: I'm advancing on the new client report, and it's nearly complete.
items.note: Provides an update on ongoing work or development, often in response to a check-in.

items.meaning: To express strong belief in one's own or a team's ability.
items.example: I'm confident in our ability to deliver this project on time and within budget.
items.plain: I strongly believe in our ability to deliver this project on time and within budget.
items.note: Conveys self-assurance and belief in capabilities.

items.meaning: To express a positive outlook regarding a future outcome.
items.example: I'm optimistic about the potential for growth in the next quarter.
items.plain: I have a positive outlook regarding the potential for growth in the next quarter.
items.note: Conveys a hopeful and positive attitude towards future developments.

items.meaning: To express absolute certainty about something.
items.example: I'm positive that we can find a solution that satisfies everyone.
items.plain: I'm absolutely certain that we can find a solution that satisfies everyone.
items.note: Conveys strong conviction and reassurance.

items.meaning: To express certainty about a collective ability to achieve something.
items.example: I'm sure we can resolve this misunderstanding with open communication.
items.plain: I'm certain we can resolve this misunderstanding with open communication.
items.note: Reassuring and collaborative, expressing confidence in team problem-solving.

items.meaning: something someone is very good at or excels in.
items.example: Your ability to simplify complex ideas is a real strength, and it really helped the team.
items.plain: You are very good at simplifying complex ideas, and it really helped the team.
items.note: Positive, specific praise. Focuses on a skill or quality.

items.meaning: to feel genuine admiration for someone's actions or qualities.
items.example: I was truly impressed by how you handled that difficult client meeting yesterday.
items.plain: I was very impressed by how you handled that difficult client meeting yesterday.
items.note: Strong, sincere praise. Often used by a manager or senior colleague.

items.meaning: to do more than what is required or expected.
items.example: The way you supported the new hires really went above and beyond, thank you.
items.plain: You supported the new hires more than was required, thank you.
items.note: Expresses appreciation for extra effort. Common in professional settings.

items.meaning: clear evidence or proof of a quality or fact.
items.example: The project's success is a testament to your meticulous planning and dedication.
items.plain: The project's success clearly shows your meticulous planning and dedication.
items.note: Formal and strong praise, often for a significant achievement.

items.meaning: reliably achieves good results or meets expectations.
items.example: Sarah consistently delivers high-quality work, which is invaluable to our team.
items.plain: Sarah reliably produces high-quality work, which is invaluable to our team.
items.note: Highlights reliability and sustained performance. Professional context.

items.meaning: an important part played in achieving something.
items.example: Your analysis was a significant contribution to our understanding of the market trends.
items.plain: Your analysis was an important part of our understanding of the market trends.
items.note: Formal, acknowledges impact. Often used in team or project reviews.

items.meaning: to behave in a way that others should imitate.
items.example: Your proactive approach to problem-solving really sets a positive example for the whole department.
items.plain: Your proactive approach to problem-solving is a good model for the whole department.
items.note: Praises leadership or influential behavior.

items.meaning: especially skilled or proficient in something.
items.example: You are particularly adept at mediating conflicts, which is a great asset.
items.plain: You are especially skilled at mediating conflicts, which is a great asset.
items.note: High-level praise for a specific skill.

items.meaning: someone who is enjoyable and easy to collaborate with.
items.example: You're always so collaborative; you're truly a pleasure to work with.
items.plain: You're always so collaborative; it's truly enjoyable to work with you.
items.note: Personal, warm praise. Focuses on interpersonal skills.

items.meaning: to praise someone for taking action independently.
items.example: I want to commend your initiative in proposing that new process improvement.
items.plain: I want to praise you for taking the initiative to propose that new process improvement.
items.note: Formal praise for proactivity.

items.meaning: a small change or modification.
items.example: I think this report just needs a minor adjustment to the formatting.
items.plain: I think this report just needs a small change to the formatting.
items.note: Understated way to suggest a small correction. Diplomatic.

items.meaning: an idea or point that should be thought about.
items.example: Here's something to consider for future presentations: perhaps fewer slides.
items.plain: Here's an idea for future presentations: perhaps fewer slides.
items.note: Gentle suggestion, not a direct criticism.

items.meaning: a small mistake made by failing to notice something.
items.example: There was a slight oversight in the budget calculations, but it's easily fixed.
items.plain: There was a small mistake in the budget calculations, but it's easily fixed.
items.note: Diplomatic way to point out a small error. Downplays blame.

items.meaning: would improve if something were added or changed.
items.example: Your proposal could benefit from a clearer executive summary.
items.plain: Your proposal would improve with a clearer executive summary.
items.note: Polite, indirect suggestion for improvement.

items.meaning: a need for greater understanding or precision.
items.example: The instructions need a bit more clarity for new users to follow them easily.
items.plain: The instructions need to be clearer for new users to follow them easily.
items.note: Gentle way to suggest something is unclear.

items.meaning: areas where improvement or development is possible.
items.example: While the project was successful, there's always room to grow in terms of efficiency.
items.plain: While the project was successful, there's always a chance to improve efficiency.
items.note: Positive framing for areas needing improvement.

items.meaning: an alternative method or strategy.
items.example: For the next phase, we might want to explore a different approach to data collection.
items.plain: For the next phase, we might want to explore an alternative method for data collection.
items.note: Suggests an alternative without directly criticizing the current one.

items.meaning: something that should be looked at or discussed again.
items.example: I think the timeline for this project might be worth revisiting.
items.plain: I think we should look at the timeline for this project again.
items.note: Polite suggestion to reconsider something.

items.meaning: an issue that causes worry or unease.
items.example: The budget overrun is a point of concern that we need to address urgently.
items.plain: The budget overrun is an issue that causes worry that we need to address urgently.
items.note: More formal than "a slight concern," indicates a more serious issue.

items.meaning: used to introduce a frank or direct statement.
items.example: To be perfectly honest, I found the presentation a little hard to follow.
items.plain: Frankly, I found the presentation a little hard to follow.
items.note: Signals directness, can soften criticism by implying sincerity.

items.meaning: expresses a general inclination to concur with an idea.
items.example: I tend to agree that we need to streamline our internal processes.
items.plain: I generally agree that we need to streamline our internal processes.
items.note: Soft way to express agreement, often with a slight reservation or nuance.

items.meaning: in my opinion or point of view.
items.example: From my perspective, the new software rollout has been quite smooth.
items.plain: In my opinion, the new software rollout has been quite smooth.
items.note: Softens a statement by presenting it as one's own view.

items.meaning: used to introduce a personal opinion or observation.
items.example: It seems to me that we're missing a key piece of information here.
items.plain: I think we're missing a key piece of information here.
items.note: Polite, indirect way to express an opinion or observation.

items.meaning: a polite way to propose an idea or course of action.
items.example: I would suggest that we allocate more resources to the marketing campaign.
items.plain: I propose that we allocate more resources to the marketing campaign.
items.note: Formal and polite way to make a suggestion.

items.meaning: a productive discussion aimed at improvement.
items.example: I hope we can have a constructive dialogue about these project challenges.
items.plain: I hope we can have a productive discussion about these project challenges.
items.note: Emphasizes a positive, problem-solving approach to discussion.

items.meaning: used to rephrase something for clarity or emphasis.
items.example: To put it another way, we need to simplify the user interface significantly.
items.plain: In other words, we need to simplify the user interface significantly.
items.note: Useful for clarifying or softening a previous statement.

items.meaning: expresses uncertainty or mild disagreement.
items.example: I'm not entirely sure that's the most efficient way to proceed.
items.plain: I'm uncertain if that's the most efficient way to proceed.
items.note: Polite way to express doubt or mild disagreement.

items.meaning: a subtle and detailed comprehension of something.
items.example: We need to develop a nuanced understanding of the cultural differences in this market.
items.plain: We need to develop a subtle and detailed understanding of the cultural differences in this market.
items.note: Suggests a need for deeper, more complex insight.

items.meaning: used to introduce a frank or direct statement.
items.example: To be quite honest, I think we underestimated the complexity of this task.
items.plain: Frankly, I think we underestimated the complexity of this task.
items.note: Similar to "to be perfectly honest," signals directness.

items.meaning: expresses gratitude for a comment or observation.
items.example: I appreciate that you pointed out the potential risks in my proposal.
items.plain: I'm grateful that you pointed out the potential risks in my proposal.
items.note: General expression of thanks for feedback, positive or constructive.

items.meaning: acknowledges that a criticism or observation is reasonable.
items.example: You're right, the timeline is ambitious; that's a fair point.
items.plain: You're right, the timeline is ambitious; that's a reasonable observation.
items.note: Concedes a point gracefully. Shows openness to feedback.

items.meaning: promises to examine a problem or issue thoroughly.
items.example: You mentioned the data discrepancy; I'll investigate that immediately.
items.plain: You mentioned the data discrepancy; I'll examine that immediately.
items.note: Professional commitment to finding facts or solutions.

items.meaning: promises to remember a piece of advice or information.
items.example: I'll keep that in mind when planning the next phase of the project.
items.plain: I'll remember that when planning the next phase of the project.
items.note: Polite way to acknowledge advice without necessarily committing to immediate action.

items.meaning: acknowledges and validates someone's worry or issue.
items.example: I understand your concern about the budget, and I'm working on solutions.
items.plain: I acknowledge your worry about the budget, and I'm working on solutions.
items.note: Empathetic response to criticism, shows active listening.

items.meaning: promises to guarantee that something will happen.
items.example: I'll ensure that the new guidelines are communicated to everyone by Friday.
items.plain: I'll guarantee that the new guidelines are communicated to everyone by Friday.
items.note: Strong commitment to action, slightly more formal than "make sure to".

items.meaning: expresses gratitude for someone's input or perspective.
items.example: Thank you for sharing your honest thoughts on the project's direction.
items.plain: I'm grateful for your honest thoughts on the project's direction.
items.note: Polite, general expression of thanks for any kind of input.

items.meaning: An exceptionally good effort or result that is noticeably better than others.
items.example: Your presentation yesterday was a standout performance; everyone was very impressed.
items.plain: Your presentation yesterday was exceptionally good; everyone was very impressed.
items.note: Strong praise, often used for a single event or achievement.

items.meaning: Always producing work or results of an excellent standard.
items.example: We've noticed your work is of consistently high quality, which is greatly valued.
items.plain: We've noticed your work is always excellent, which is greatly valued.
items.note: Highlights reliability and excellence over time.

items.meaning: Something that adds significant worth or benefit to a project or team.
items.example: Your insights during the meeting were a valuable contribution to our strategy discussion.
items.plain: Your insights during the meeting were very helpful for our strategy discussion.
items.note: Standard, positive feedback. Can be used for ideas or effort.

items.meaning: Showed effective qualities of guiding and inspiring others.
items.example: You really demonstrated strong leadership in managing that difficult client project.
items.plain: You really showed effective leadership in managing that difficult client project.
items.note: Specific praise for leadership skills.

items.meaning: Someone or something that brings honor or respect to a group or organization.
items.example: Your professionalism makes you a credit to the entire department.
items.plain: Your professionalism makes the entire department look good.
items.note: Formal and sincere praise.

items.meaning: Someone or something that is very valuable and beneficial.
items.example: Your problem-solving skills are a significant asset to the team.
items.plain: Your problem-solving skills are very valuable to the team.
items.note: Strong, formal praise, emphasizing value.

items.meaning: Serving as an excellent model or example; outstanding.
items.example: Your dedication to client satisfaction is truly exemplary.
items.plain: Your dedication to client satisfaction is an excellent example for others.
items.note: High praise, often for behavior or attitude.

items.meaning: Always performs better than what is required or anticipated.
items.example: Your work consistently exceeds expectations, which is fantastic.
items.plain: Your work is always better than what is expected, which is fantastic.
items.note: Strong praise for sustained high performance.

items.meaning: Someone or something that has a good effect on others or a situation.
items.example: Your calm demeanor is a positive influence on the whole team during stressful periods.
items.plain: Your calm demeanor has a good effect on the whole team during stressful periods.
items.note: Praises impact on others' morale or performance.

items.meaning: Considered to be very important or useful.
items.example: Your contributions to the project are highly valued by everyone.
items.plain: Everyone considers your contributions to the project to be very important.
items.note: Standard, sincere praise, often used in formal settings.

items.meaning: A helpful idea for improvement, offered in a positive way.
items.example: I have a constructive suggestion regarding the project timeline, if you're open to hearing it.
items.plain: I have a helpful idea for improving the project timeline, if you're open to hearing it.
items.note: Signals that the feedback is intended to be helpful, not just critical.

items.meaning: A polite way to bring something to someone's attention again.
items.example: Just a gentle reminder that the report is due by end of day tomorrow.
items.plain: Please remember that the report is due by end of day tomorrow.
items.note: Softens a request or a reminder of an obligation.

items.meaning: A possible aspect or part that could be developed or improved.
items.example: This could be a potential area where we might face some resistance.
items.plain: This could be an aspect where we might face some resistance.
items.note: Hedges a suggestion for improvement or a foreseen problem.

items.meaning: A small change or modification.
items.example: We might need to make a slight adjustment to the budget for next quarter.
items.plain: We might need to make a small change to the budget for next quarter.
items.note: Understated way to suggest a change, implying it's not major.

items.meaning: A warning or advice to be careful about something.
items.example: Just a word of caution about relying too heavily on those preliminary figures.
items.plain: I just want to warn you about relying too heavily on those preliminary figures.
items.note: Polite way to offer a warning or express a reservation.

items.meaning: I would cautiously suggest or state, often when expressing an opinion that might be unexpected.
items.example: I'd venture to say that the new strategy might not be as effective as we hope.
items.plain: I would cautiously suggest that the new strategy might not be as effective as we hope.
items.note: Hedges a strong opinion, making it sound more polite or less assertive.

items.meaning: It would be wise or sensible to do something.
items.example: Given the current market, it might be prudent to delay the launch.
items.plain: Given the current market, it would be wise to delay the launch.
items.note: Formal and cautious suggestion.

items.meaning: To provide comments or suggestions for improvement.
items.example: I wanted to offer some feedback on your presentation, if you have a moment.
items.plain: I wanted to give you some comments on your presentation, if you have a moment.
items.note: Standard, polite opening for giving feedback.

items.meaning: Done with good motives, even if the outcome isn't perfect.
items.example: I know the decision was made with the best intentions, but it caused some issues.
items.plain: I know the decision was made with good motives, but it caused some issues.
items.note: Acknowledges good motives before delivering criticism.

items.meaning: A small lack of connection or understanding between different parts or ideas.
items.example: There seems to be a slight disconnect between the project goals and the proposed timeline.
items.plain: There seems to be a small lack of connection between the project goals and the proposed timeline.
items.note: Diplomatic way to point out an inconsistency or lack of alignment.

items.meaning: A point in a process where progress is likely to slow down or stop.
items.example: I foresee a potential bottleneck in the approval process if we don't streamline it.
items.plain: I foresee a point where the approval process is likely to slow down if we don't streamline it.
items.note: Identifies a future problem area.

items.meaning: Something that needs to be dealt with before other things.
items.example: I think addressing client concerns should be a matter of priority.
items.plain: I think addressing client concerns should be dealt with before other things.
items.note: Emphasizes urgency or importance.

items.meaning: I am somewhat disposed to propose or recommend something.
items.example: I'm inclined to suggest we re-evaluate our approach to market entry.
items.plain: I am somewhat disposed to propose we re-evaluate our approach to market entry.
items.note: Polite, slightly hesitant way to offer a suggestion.

items.meaning: Suggests that something is a good idea to think about.
items.example: It might be worth considering alternative suppliers for this component.
items.plain: It could be a good idea to think about alternative suppliers for this component.
items.note: Gentle suggestion, inviting discussion.

items.meaning: A minor error in comprehension or interpretation.
items.example: I think there might be a slight misunderstanding about the project scope.
items.plain: I think there might be a minor error in understanding about the project scope.
items.note: Diplomatic way to correct someone or point out an error.

items.meaning: A new or alternative way of looking at a situation or problem.
items.example: Perhaps we could approach this from a different angle to find a solution.
items.plain: Perhaps we could approach this in a new way to find a solution.
items.note: Suggests exploring new perspectives.

items.meaning: A polite way to thank someone for their contribution or suggestions.
items.example: I appreciate your input on the new marketing strategy; it gives us a lot to consider.
items.plain: Thank you for your suggestions on the new marketing strategy; it gives us a lot to consider.
items.note: Standard, polite acknowledgement of feedback.

items.meaning: A polite way to say you will think about the suggestion, without committing to it.
items.example: That's an interesting idea; I'll certainly consider that for the next phase.
items.plain: That's an interesting idea; I will definitely think about that for the next phase.
items.note: Polite, non-committal response, often used when you need time to evaluate.

items.text: I'm glad you brought that up
items.form: I'm glad you brought that up
items.meaning: Expresses appreciation for someone raising a topic or concern.
items.example: I'm glad you brought that up, as it's something we've been discussing internally.
items.plain: I'm happy you mentioned that, as it's something we've been discussing internally.
items.note: Shows openness and willingness to discuss the issue.

items.meaning: Willing to provide more details or explain something further.
items.example: If anything was unclear, I'm happy to elaborate on my points.
items.plain: If anything was unclear, I'm willing to explain my points further.
items.note: Offers to clarify, showing helpfulness and openness.

items.meaning: Expresses a strong dedication to making things better.
items.example: I understand your feedback and I'm committed to improving my time management.
items.plain: I understand your feedback and I am dedicated to making my time management better.
items.note: Strong, positive response to criticism, showing accountability.

items.meaning: Thanks someone for being direct and truthful, even if the feedback is difficult.
items.example: It was tough to hear, but I'm grateful for your honesty about my performance.
items.plain: It was tough to hear, but I appreciate you being direct about my performance.
items.note: Acknowledges difficult feedback positively.

items.meaning: Indicates active listening and recording of information.
items.example: Please continue, I'm taking notes to ensure I capture all your points.
items.plain: Please continue, I am writing down what you say to ensure I capture all your points.
items.note: Shows engagement and seriousness in receiving feedback.

items.meaning: I will ensure that I include or integrate something.
items.example: That's a good idea; I'll make sure to incorporate it into the next draft.
items.plain: That's a good idea; I will ensure I include it into the next draft.
items.note: Strong commitment to act on feedback.

items.meaning: I am willing to listen to or consider something.
items.example: I'm open to hearing any further suggestions you might have.
items.plain: I am willing to listen to any further suggestions you might have.
items.note: Invites more feedback, showing receptiveness.

items.meaning: I am very eager to acquire new knowledge or skills.
items.example: I'm keen to learn how I can improve my presentation skills.
items.plain: I am very eager to learn how I can improve my presentation skills.
items.note: Expresses enthusiasm for personal development.

items.meaning: I am continuously searching for or seeking something.
items.example: I'm always looking for ways to streamline our workflow.
items.plain: I am continuously searching for ways to streamline our workflow.
items.note: Shows proactive attitude towards improvement.

items.text: I'll ensure it doesn't happen again
items.form: I'll ensure it doesn't happen again
items.meaning: I will make certain that this mistake or issue is not repeated.
items.example: I understand the error; I'll ensure it doesn't happen again.
items.plain: I understand the error; I will make certain it is not repeated.
items.note: Strong commitment to corrective action.
